newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian share volume dips, Hansapank active.
newsitem.headline: Estonian share volume dips, Hansapank active.

text.p: Volumes on the Estonian stock market were a touch lower on Wednesday and leading bank Hansapank was the most active stock on the main list.
Official list turnover was 6.99 million kroons and the Tallinn stock exchange index rose 0.77 percent to 97.94.
Hansapank traded 4.8 million kroons and closed at 98.25 versus 96.80 kroons yesterday.

Other shares on the main list were quiet and market attention was focussed on the free market, where plastics maker Norma released its nine month earnings of 36 million kroons and forecast earnings of 48 million kroons for the year.
Free market turnover was 5.5 million kroons and Norma traded 1.03 million kroons and rose to 22.60 kroons from 21.80.
Tallinn Department Store was an active 1.3 million kroons and rose to 53.05 from 52.89 kroons. The Rakvere meat processing plant also posted a gain, rising to 3.82 kroons from 3.35.
Hansapank equities chief Tonu Pekk said he was generally optimistic about the market.
"In general the market is going up and we are seeing more institutions prepared to invest in Estonia," he said.
The market tomorrow will see the start of trading in computer company Pennu, which will be the first stock on a new secondary list for small and medium-sized companies.
